brief.topic: Why the Last Sticker Takes So Long

s01: One space left in the album.
Another packet opens,
and it is a sticker we already have.
Then another duplicate.
Completing a collection often feels slower near the end.
There is a gentle mathematical reason.
Imagine six equally likely stickers,
one in each packet.
Every packet is independent.
Our first sticker is always new.
With three spaces still empty,
three of the six possible stickers help.
The chance of a new one is one half,
so the average wait is two packets.
With just one space empty,
only one of the six possibilities helps.
Now the average wait is six packets.
That does not mean the sixth packet is guaranteed
to finish the album.
A fresh packet still has the same one in six chance.
To see where the average comes from,
call the remaining wait E.
We always open one packet.
Five times out of six,
we are back where we started,
still waiting an average of E more.
So E equals one plus five sixths of E.
Subtract those five sixths.
One sixth of E is one,
and E is six.
Adding the average waits
for all six new stickers gives fourteen point seven packets
for a complete album.
That is an average over many collections,
not a promise about yours.
Near the finish,
fewer outcomes count as progress.
Sometimes slowing down is simply part of the landscape.
